preamble: Click loss in East Kalahari Khoe (Shua and Tshwa clusters: Cara, ǀXaise, Danisi, Deti, Kua, Tsua). Here the palatal click series of Proto-Kalahari Khoe has been largely replaced, mostly by non-click palatal consonants (Tsua and southern Kua still keep some palatal clicks), a regular sound change documented by Traill & Vossen (1997). Sands & Gunnink (2019) note that Khoe click loss increases with distance from the Kalahari core and may be sped up by contact with languages that lack clicks. Western languages such as ǀGwi and Kxoe, and Ts'ixa, which often has the click (partly through contact with Kxoe), keep it, e.g. ǀGwi ǂéē (Nakagawa 2006), Ts'ixa ǂé 'ear'. The glottalized palatal click *ǂʼ lost its click and kept only its glottal closure [ʔ], usually followed by a palatal glide y [j] that continues the palatal place. All East Kalahari varieties except Ts'ixa show this (Ts'ixa ǂʼã́ 'wind', ǂʼũ̌ 'eat'). The source segment is strictly the glottalized click [ǂʼ]. Forms follow the GLD's transcription (Vossen 1997 data). In that system ɕ and ʓ are palatal (alveolo-palatal) affricates [tɕ, dʑ], y is [j], and ʸ marks palatalization.
